issues.description: Element: Animal.getName() and Animal.setName(String). The problem statement (instructions) explicitly tell students to implement the name getter and setter with protected visibility to "prevent unauthorized external access while allowing subclass inheritance." (problem_statement.md lines 87-89). The solution implementation declares these methods as public: public String getName() (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java lines 10-12) and public void setName(String) (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java lines 14-16). This mismatch between the textual requirement (protected) and the reference implementation (public) can confuse students about the intended access level and whether tests expect protected or public methods.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the visibility consistent. Either change the solution's method signatures to protected (protected String getName() and protected void setName(String)) and update the template accordingly, or update the problem statement and UML to indicate public visibility is acceptable. Ensure the chosen visibility is reflected in the UML, the textual instructions, the template code, and the reference solution so students are not left to guess the intended access level.

issues.description: Element: Animal(String) constructor. The UML in the problem statement denotes the Animal constructor with protected visibility (UML uses '#' for the constructor: "# Animal(String): void" — problem_statement.md lines 26-31). The solution implements the constructor as public: public Animal(String name) (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java lines 6-8). This discrepancy between the UML-provided visibility (protected) and the reference implementation (public) may confuse students about whether the abstract base class constructor should be protected or public.
issues.suggestedFix: Align constructor visibility across artifacts. Either change the solution constructor to protected Animal(String name) to match the UML, and update the template accordingly, or update the UML/problem statement to explicitly allow a public constructor. Ensure the constructor visibility is consistent in the UML diagram, textual instructions, template code, and reference solution to avoid ambiguity for students.
